sizeClasses.name: wide
sizeClasses.teach: the full body width, 4 or more lines: lists, checklists, steppers, reading

sizeClasses.name: band
sizeClasses.teach: the full width, 1-3 lines: a formula line, facts, a caption, a short note

sizeClasses.name: column
sizeClasses.teach: a narrow column of 8 lines: a list or steppers with short labels

sizeClasses.name: pane
sizeClasses.teach: a wider column of 2-8 lines: detail text, facts, a timer, a formula line

sizeClasses.name: plate
sizeClasses.teach: one image box of at most 288x144: a Graphic or a picture

containers.name: rule
containers.holds: the header rule; U+0300 at brightness 0

containers.name: cursor
containers.holds: the split rail's column head, in the band under the rule (G2 ride 4)

containers.name: dim
containers.holds: the position cue on line 0 and every dim line of every Region

containers.name: bright
containers.holds: the focused driver row and every bright line of every Region

choose.what: One block that fills the display: a set they pick from by name, items they tick off, values they set, or one thing they read or page through. Nothing beside it changes with the row they are on.
choose.not_for: A set where each row's detail, a total or a timer has to show beside or under the row they are on; a picture or a chart
examples: which of these three should I take
what's left to pack
ten minutes till the board call — what do I actually need to know

frames.name: stack
frames.teach: a Region on top, a short band under it that follows the row

choose.what: A set they pick from, tick or adjust on top, with a line or two under it that follows the row they are on or adds it up: its detail, a running total, a countdown.
choose.not_for: Detail longer than a couple of lines for each row; a picture or a chart; one block with nothing under it
examples: what's the shape of today
split the bill four ways and let me nudge the tip
what am I doing in the next hour, and when do I move

frames.card: frame stack: top (drives, wide), bottom (follows, band)

frames.name: split
frames.teach: a narrow column on the left, a pane on the right that follows the row

choose.what: Named options side by side: a short list in a narrow column, and a wider pane that shows the one they are on with its facts or a number worked out for it, so they can compare before they choose.
choose.not_for: Long names that need the full width; a picture or a chart; one block to read
examples: compare these three hotels for me
which of the two flights is better value
show the three plans and what each costs per month

frames.card: frame split: rail (drives, column), pane (follows, pane)

frames.name: plate
frames.teach: one image box, a caption band under it, nothing to pick

choose.what: A picture or a small chart is the answer, with a short caption under it. Nothing to pick.
choose.not_for: A set to pick from; an answer that reads better as words
examples: just the bird and its name, nothing else
how's my step count trending this week
show me the logo

frames.name: rail-plate
frames.teach: a narrow column on the left, a picture and a short pane on the right that follow the row

choose.what: A short list of named things in a narrow column, each with its own picture or chart beside it, so they browse by looking at each one.
choose.not_for: One picture with nothing to pick; long names that need the full width
examples: show me the three paint colours and let me flick through them
which of these plants is the monstera
the four dashboards, one chart each

frames.card: frame rail-plate: rail (drives, column), plate (image), foot (follows, pane)

roots.name: state
roots.teach: the surface's own state on the phone: stepper values, marks

roots.name: data
roots.teach: read-only data a template input, a refresh or a cron tick supplied

roots.name: sel
roots.teach: a column of the driver's current row, by its `cols` name

roots.name: prev
roots.teach: the value a data path held before the last refresh; null until the second

roots.name: ref
roots.teach: a `let` name, or a timer reading such as pasta.remaining

operators.name: div
operators.teach: a / b; dividing by zero gives null

operators.name: round
operators.teach: round(x) or round(x, digits); halves round away from zero

operators.name: num
operators.teach: reads numeric text such as '140' or '-2.5' as a number; anything else gives null

operators.name: eq
operators.teach: a == b, same value and type

operators.name: lt
operators.teach: a < b; false when either is null

operators.name: and
operators.teach: and(a, b): true when all are true

operators.name: or
operators.teach: or(a, b): true when any is true

operators.name: coalesce
operators.teach: the first value that is not null, such as coalesce(note, 'none')

operators.name: concat
operators.teach: joins text; format numbers first with fmt

operators.name: clip
operators.teach: clip(text, bytes): cuts text to that many bytes

operators.name: count
operators.teach: count(pack) counts a list's rows; count(pack, 'ticked') the rows the wearer ticked

operators.name: sum
operators.teach: sum(cart, 'price') totals a column; sum(cart, 'price', 'ticked') only the ticked rows

fmtStyles.name: num
fmtStyles.teach: 1,234.5; decimals 0-10, else 0 for a whole number and 2 otherwise

fmtStyles.name: money
fmtStyles.teach: the ISO code first: EUR 420, EUR 1,234.50

fmtStyles.name: dur
fmtStyles.teach: milliseconds as m:ss under an hour, h:mm:ss from an hour

behaviours.name: step
behaviours.teach: moves a number by `by` between `min` and `max`; clamps at the ends, or wraps if asked

behaviours.name: select
behaviours.teach: moves to the next or previous entry of a closed list of at most 20

behaviours.name: expand
behaviours.teach: shows or hides a component's detail; view state, like focus

behaviours.name: countdown
behaviours.teach: counts down for a duration, or until a data time; at zero it shows 0:00 and wakes nobody

behaviours.name: elapsed
behaviours.teach: counts up from its start, or since a data time

behaviours.name: sort
behaviours.teach: orders a table's rows by one column, low to high, or high to low after a -; view state, like focus

behaviours.name: keep
behaviours.teach: a let with on keeps a value: it starts at be, and each named action's tap sets it to that action's formula

behaviours.name: append
behaviours.teach: a list with on and row adds that row, one formula per col, on each tap of the named action, up to its 20 rows

props.name: frame
props.teach: the Layout Frame's name

props.name: title
props.teach: the heading; a composed surface always has one (F7)

kinds.teach: starts a surface; comes first and carries the title (G4)

props.name: let
props.teach: the derived value's name

props.name: be
props.teach: its formula, such as nights*rate

props.name: on
props.teach: action:formula|action:formula; keeps the value: it starts at be, and each action's tap sets it to its formula

props.name: remove
props.teach: true removes the name at the commit (G10)

kinds.teach: declares a named value other records read by name (R8, G8)

props.name: id
props.teach: the stable handle a later turn patches by; a stepper's id is its value's name

props.name: c
props.teach: the component's name

props.name: in
props.teach: the Region it sits in; components in one Region stack in record order

props.name: show
props.teach: a test such as total>budget; hidden content keeps its space; never on the driver's component (R15)

props.name: remove
props.teach: true removes the component at the commit; the ones below move up (G10)

kinds.teach: places a component; a later turn's record with a known id changes only the fields it names

driver.name: actions
driver.teach: id:Label|id:Label; each is a last row of the driver that wakes you with its id

driver.name: controls
driver.teach: run:<timer id>|reset:<timer id>; rows that start, pause or reset a timer and wake nobody

props.name: text
props.teach: the text, or =formula such as =sel.detail; the body may hold it instead

choose.what: A short set of named things: they pick one by its name, and the name alone is enough — including when more about the one they pick sits behind it and they open it AFTER choosing. Also the right shape when the assistant proposes a set of named things and the wearer is approving the set.
choose.not_for: Rows they have to weigh against each other, where the reason has to be visible before they can decide
examples: start me at the three categories and let me open whichever looks right
which services has the Greggs, Keele or Sandbach?
group my photo folders by month, but check with me first

choose.what: Items THEY tick off as they go, in any order they like, where the list is theirs and the point is what is left.
choose.not_for: A procedure the assistant walks them through one step at a time, waiting between steps. That is a document they page through, not a list they own.
examples: the leaving-the-house routine
what's left to pack

presets.name: list_with_details

choose.what: A set of rows where each row's reason, trade-off or outcome has to be visible BEFORE they choose, because the labels alone would not let them decide. Also the right shape for the shape of a day or an hour, and for an account of several separate things, where each line is a thing and the detail is how it goes.
choose.not_for: A set of named things they browse and open one at a time; a brief read straight through in order; a single verdict about one thing
examples: what did I actually get through today
what's the shape of today
what am I doing in the next hour, and when do I move

presets.teach: V1 list_with_details_surface: a list with a text reading sel.detail

choose.what: One thing they read or glance at: a value, a verdict, a short note, one named label, a countdown that ticks on its own. Nothing to pick. A single verdict about one journey or one activity belongs here however many facts fed into it.
choose.not_for: A set of options they choose between; an account of several separate things that each deserve their own line; the shape of their day or their next hour, where every entry is its own row
examples: is it worth taking the bike in this morning
how's the surf looking
just the bird and its name, nothing else
twenty-five minutes head-down, starting now

choose.what: One longer thing they move through screen by screen with nothing to choose: a briefing they absorb before something starts, a summary read straight through in order, or a procedure where only the current step is on screen.
choose.not_for: Short answers, picks, the shape of a day, or a single value that keeps ticking on its own
examples: ten minutes till the board call — what do I actually need to know
talk me through bleeding the radiator, one step at a time
give me the gist a bit at a time

renderShape.lead: Put it on the glasses. Any ONE of these is enough:
renderShape.not_for: Idle curiosity or banter with nothing to act on

triggers.label: they pick from a set
examples: which of these three should I take
quick, 180 fan or 200?

triggers.wording: they will glance at a value or a verdict and act on it
triggers.label: a value or verdict to act on
examples: is it worth surfing Lyall Bay this afternoon
just your gut, one word — the 7:40 or the 9:15 for my sister's flight

triggers.wording: they will watch something change on its own
triggers.label: something that changes on its own
examples: twenty-five minutes head-down, starting now

triggers.wording: they need a visual (a chart, an image, a named thing beside its picture)
triggers.label: something visual
examples: just the bird and its name, nothing else

triggers.wording: they asked to be taken through a procedure, with only the current step kept on screen
triggers.label: a procedure, one step on screen

triggers.label: something shown at a later time
examples: nudge me to take the tablets at eight tonight

triggers.label: an account of what happened

triggers.label: a proposal for them to approve

chatShapes.label: a spoken reply is the whole answer
chatShapes.what: A spoken reply is the whole answer: idle curiosity, banter, an opinion, a fact they hear once and do not need to hold. This includes a yes-or-no verdict on a question with two sides to it, heard once, with no named options to pick between and nothing to keep.
chatShapes.not_for: A reading of the wearer's own numbers, work or day; a one-word pick between named options they want kept on screen; something they will act on at a later moment (a reminder, a nudge, a time to leave); an account of what they did; a name they need to recall; a reading they will look at more than once
examples: why do cats knead?
what's the difference between a mutex and a semaphore?
is two grand a fair price for a 2012 Golf, yes or no?

chatShapes.label: the long version, listened to
chatShapes.what: They explicitly asked for the long version or the full story AND said they would rather listen than look.
chatShapes.not_for: A procedure where only the current step is on screen. Even when they say 'talk me through it', each step has to stay put on screen until they move on, so that is a surface.
examples: talk me through how a heat pump works, I'm just listening

chatShapes.label: a fact only the wearer holds
chatShapes.what: The assistant cannot produce any useful answer until the wearer supplies a fact that ONLY the wearer holds.
chatShapes.not_for: A request the assistant can answer with a reasonable default. This includes a request where the wearer asked to be checked with before it is applied: the proposal IS the answer, and it is shown to them for approval.
examples: send it to the usual address

namedDestination.wording: they named where the answer goes, in chat or on the glasses; that wins over every trigger, and a bare "show me" or "put it up" names no destination
namedDestination.label: a named destination wins
examples: just tell me in chat
no need to render this one
put this on the glasses
on the display, not in chat

instructions.question: The wearer of smart glasses (small heads-up display, about five short lines) said this to their assistant. What should the assistant do with its answer?
instructions.focus: Judge by what the wearer will DO with the answer, not by how much content there is.

instructions.question: If this were put on the glasses, which surface fits? Decide by what the wearer does with it, never by how much content it holds.
If this were put on the glasses as one screen, which layout fits it? Decide by what the wearer does with it, never by how much content it holds.
If a small chart were drawn for this, which one element fits the shape of the reading? Pick none when words, a pick, or a live-ticking number is the right answer.
Does the wearer want this to happen again on a schedule or keep updating, rather than once right now?
Is this one thing the assistant answers now and is then finished with, or something the wearer asked to have run again later on its own?
instructions.focus: Judge what the wearer asked for, not how useful a standing task would be. Saving something they asked for once is a cost they did not agree to.

true.what: Asks for it every morning, daily, whenever it changes, keep watching

template.what: Answered once, now. When the wearer looks away it is finished, even if the answer keeps ticking while they are watching it.
template.not_for: A standing arrangement the wearer asked to keep running after this moment

what did I get through today

task.what: The wearer asked for it to run again later by itself: on a schedule, at a named time, or whenever some condition changes.
task.not_for: A single question they want answered this once
examples: I'd like it every morning
nudge me at eight tonight
tell me if the build goes red while I'm cooking
